-기는요.es: qué va, no es para tanto
-기는요.en: It's not that big a deal.

잘하기는요.es: qué va, no se me da tan bien
잘하기는요.en: I'm not so good at it.

배울 게 많아요.en: I have a lot to learn.

texto: **A/V-기는요** puede usarse como respuesta para rechazar o rebajar un elogio o una suposición: 잘하다 → **잘하기는요** (qué va, no se me da tan bien), 좋다 → **좋기는요** (qué va, no es tan bueno). The nuance depends on the conversation.
I have a lot to learn.
At the end of an answer, **-기는요** corrects or minimizes what another person just said. do**-기는 하지만** grants something and continues with a contrast:

frases.es: Se le da muy bien cocinar comida coreana.
frases.en: He's very good at cooking Korean food.

frases.es: Qué va. Todavía me queda mucho por aprender.
frases.en: No way. I still have a lot to learn.
analisis: I'm not so good at it.
I still have a lot to learn.

frases.es: Aun así, la comida está rica.

bloques.pregunta: What is «잘하기는요»'s nuance in response to a praise?

opciones.explicacion: The person rejects or minimizes what they have just said to him.

opciones.texto: I presume to do better than the others.
opciones.explicacion: It is not the nuance of this answer.

opciones.texto: He says he's not gonna learn.
opciones.explicacion: That would be the way it is.

bloques.pregunta: No, I'm not that good at it.

opciones.explicacion: It means «He's doing good.» without correcting the praise.
It means «He did well.» in the past.

opciones.texto: No, it's harder than I thought.
opciones.explicacion: The idea that it was easy is corrected.

opciones.texto: It's easy and I didn't think about it.
opciones.explicacion: That doesn't correspond to the contrast.

opciones.texto: He thinks he still has a lot to learn.
opciones.explicacion: In this context, the Commission has also taken the view that there is still much to be learned.

opciones.texto: He thinks he already knows everything.
opciones.explicacion: That would be the only way.
That would be the only way to go.

bloques.traduccion: I still have a lot to learn.
bloques.explicacion: I have a lot to learn.

bloques.pregunta: What's the difference between «읽기는 했지만» and «읽기는요»?

opciones.texto: The first form gives something and adds a contrast; the second can respond by minimizing an affirmation.
opciones.explicacion: - It links a concession with another idea.

opciones.texto: They mean exactly the same thing.
opciones.explicacion: They change the function and the position.

opciones.texto: The first is future and the second is past.
opciones.explicacion: No form expresses itself in those times.
I couldn't read it until the end.
It means I'm done reading it.
